sections.history: Thalaichangadu, in the Tharangambadi taluk near Poompuhar, is a Paadal Petra Sthalam of the Kaveri's southern bank, its Shiva hymned in the Tevaram by Tirugnana Sambandar; by one reckoning it is the shrine counted among those of the lower delta coast. Temple tradition ascribes its founding to the Chola king Kochengat Chola, with the stone structure of the Chola period and later. A Vishnu temple nearby, Thalai Sanga Nanmathiyam, is a Divya Desam, and the two shrines share a single sthala legend.
sections.architecture: The temple is a Dravidian coastal shrine with Sankaranyeswarar in the sanctum, worshipped in the Somaskanda form (Shiva with Uma and Skanda), and the goddess Soundara Nayaki — also called Bruhath Sundarambikai — in her own shrine. The sacred tank is the Sangu Theertham, 'the tank of the conch,' and the sthala vriksham is the purasu (flame-of-the-forest). A Nandi and the parivara devatas complete the plan.
sections.legends: The great legend of the place tells that Vishnu worshipped Shiva here with deep devotion, and that from this worship he received the Panchajanya, his divine conch (sangu). From the conch — sangu — and its head — talai — the village takes its name, Thalaichangadu, and its tank is the Sangu Theertham. The puranam is bound to that of the Valampuranathar temple at nearby Melaperumpallam, where the conch's turning is remembered, and to the Divya Desam of Thalai Sanga Nanmathiyam close by.
sections.festivals: The temple keeps Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship. As a coastal delta shrine linked to a Divya Desam, it draws both Shaiva and Vaishnava pilgrims who honour the legend of the conch.
sections.experience: Thalaichangadu offers the pilgrim a rare coastal shrine where the stories of Shiva and Vishnu meet. Before Sankaranyeswarar in his Somaskanda grace and Soundara Nayaki, beside the Sangu Theertham and within sight of the Divya Desam, the visitor stands at the 'forest of the conch,' where Vishnu is said to have won his Panchajanya — a place layered with the devotion of two great traditions.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Thalaichangadu is in Tharangambadi taluk, about 22 km from Mayiladuthurai and 16 km from Sirkazhi, near Poompuhar on the coast. Mayiladuthurai or Sirkazhi are the nearest rail heads, with buses and taxis to the village; the Thalai Sanga Nanmathiyam Divya Desam is less than a kilometre away.
